corrections.old: Bees and hornets. Both nest on the rock face. … Attacks are uncommon, but the upper stairs are sometimes closed for a while after a nest is disturbed.
corrections.new: Giant honeybees nest on the rock face; signs call them hornets … In August 2024, 22 visitors needed hospital treatment after part of a nest fell in strong wind, and the site closed for a while. If you are allergic to stings, carry your medication.
corrections.reason: An entomologist quoted by Mongabay identifies the insects as giant honeybees (Apis dorsata), though signs say hornets; the 2024 incident shows attacks can be serious and lead to closures.

newExperiences.name: Pidurangala Rock climb
newExperiences.shortDescription: Climb the rock next to Sigiriya, past a temple and a brick reclining Buddha, for the classic view of Lion Rock, often at sunrise.
newExperiences.details: Pidurangala rises about 1 km north of Lion Rock. A path from the working temple at its foot climbs past a large brick reclining Buddha to a final boulder scramble where you need your hands; most people reach the top in 30–45 minutes. The temple charges its own fee and asks visitors to cover shoulders and knees. For sunrise, bring a torch and shoes with good grip.
newExperiences.notes: No official source (the temple runs it; not CCF). Fee reported as LKR 500–1,000; opening times vary (about 5 am). Owner: pre-dawn start possible? 'where' not needed (about 1 km from Lion Rock).

newExperiences.name: Elephant safari: Minneriya, Kaudulla or Hurulu
newExperiences.shortDescription: An afternoon jeep safari to see wild elephants graze the old reservoir beds; drivers pick the park on the day. Sightings are never guaranteed.
newExperiences.details: Minneriya and Kaudulla national parks and Hurulu Eco Park share the same herds, so drivers choose the park on the day. From about July to October elephants graze the drying reservoir beds, usually peaking around August and September at Minneriya; numbers vary with water levels. Most safaris last about 3 hours in the afternoon. Ask your driver to keep a good distance and not to crowd the herds.
newExperiences.where: Minneriya, Kaudulla or Hurulu Eco Park, about 30–60 minutes by road from Sigiriya
newExperiences.season: Best about July–October; usually peaks around August–September
newExperiences.notes: This is the experience id of the new guide /experiences/minneriya-elephant-safari/ (please add it to experiences.mjs so the guide's experience: resolves). Listed under Sigiriya because Sigiriya/Habarana is the usual base and where most jeeps are hired; all three areas are 30–60 min away. Hurulu is a Forest Department eco park, not a national park. Never guaranteed; numbers collapsed around 2019–2021 when the tanks were kept full. Kind: excursion, following the brief's own Minneriya example; it is also an activity (jeep safari).

newExperiences.name: Ritigala forest monastery
newExperiences.shortDescription: Walk a paved forest path through the ruins of an ascetic monastery on the lower slopes of Ritigala, a mountain reserve north of Habarana.
newExperiences.details: Ritigala rises to 766 m above the dry-zone plains. The mountain is a strict nature reserve, but the monastery ruins on its lower slopes are open. Monks lived here from about the 1st century BC, and a stone path leads through shaded forest past a reservoir, a monastery hospital and paired stone platforms joined by bridges. Allow 2–3 hours on site; it has its own ticket and is rarely crowded.
newExperiences.where: Ritigala, about an hour by road north of Sigiriya via Habarana
newExperiences.notes: CCF price list includes a Ritigala ticket (USD 6 full); 11,267 foreign visitors in 2025 (SLTDA). Some resellers say entry is now only with a guide: unconfirmed, re-check. Could also sit under anuradhapura (about 43 km), but Sigiriya/Habarana is closer. Drive time is an estimate.

newExperiences.name: Village tour near Habarana
newExperiences.shortDescription: A packaged walk through paddy fields, a short boat crossing of a village tank and a home-cooked rice-and-curry lunch. Organised for visitors.
newExperiences.details: Village tours around Habarana and Sigiriya, the best known at Hiriwadunna, follow a set routine: a walk along paddy bunds, a crossing of the village tank in a small boat and a rice-and-curry lunch cooked over a wood fire in a village home. They are commercial and partly staged, but the farmland and food are real. Most take 2–3 hours, often around lunchtime.
newExperiences.where: Hiriwadunna and other villages around Habarana, about 20–30 minutes from Sigiriya
newExperiences.notes: No independent media source; description from a University of Jaffna field-study report (Oct 2025, Divisional Secretariat-run community tourism with a bullock cart, house visits, lake boat and village walk) and operator listings. Deliberately does not mention the bullock-cart ride. Kind: activity although Hiriwadunna is about 20–30 min away; use 'excursion' if you prefer. Owner: offered/recommended?

newExperiences.name: Sri Lankan cooking class
newExperiences.shortDescription: Cook a rice-and-curry meal with a local family near Sigiriya: several curries and a coconut sambol, often in clay pots over a wood fire.
newExperiences.details: Family kitchens around Sigiriya run hands-on classes. You usually help prepare rice, three or four vegetable or lentil curries and a coconut sambol, often in clay pots over a wood fire, and some start with a garden or market visit. Most last about 3 hours and end with eating what you cooked. Classes are commercial and vary, so mention dietary needs when booking.
newExperiences.notes: Only commercial listings exist for this kind of activity (no official source). Keep only if the owner wants a food option; otherwise merge into the village tour card.

newExperiences.name: Dambulla cave temple
newExperiences.shortDescription: Climb to five painted cave shrines filled with Buddha images, a working temple and UNESCO World Heritage Site above Dambulla town.
newExperiences.details: Stone steps climb the side of a granite outcrop to five cave shrines with more than 150 statues, including a 14 m reclining Buddha, under ceilings painted with scenes from the Buddha's life. The caves have been used for worship since the 1st century BC and are still an active temple. Buy the ticket at the foot before you climb, cover shoulders and knees, and allow 1–2 hours.
newExperiences.notes: Category culture, as for the Kandy temple card (a working temple). Ticket seller unclear (see ownerQuestions).

newExperiences.name: Nalanda Gedige
newExperiences.shortDescription: A small stone shrine of about the 8th–10th century that blends a South Indian temple plan with Buddhist use, near the road to Kandy.
newExperiences.details: This stone image house follows a South Indian Hindu temple plan but was used for Buddhist worship, and its weathered carvings mix both traditions. It was dismantled and rebuilt on higher ground when the Bowatenne reservoir was built. A visit takes about half an hour, so it fits a stop on the drive between Dambulla and Kandy.
newExperiences.where: Nalanda, about 25 km south of Dambulla, just off the Kandy road
newExperiences.notes: Relocation dated 1970s or 1980s depending on source; the card gives no date. Could equally sit under kandy (about 70 km).

newExperiences.name: Popham's Arboretum and night loris walk
newExperiences.shortDescription: Walk quiet trails through a restored patch of dry-zone forest, or join a guided night walk to look for slender lorises.
newExperiences.details: Sam Popham began restoring this scrubland as dry-zone forest in 1963; it now belongs to the National Institute of Fundamental Studies, which reopened it for visitors in 2023. Marked trails make a quiet hour's walk by day. Guided night walks of about 1–1.5 hours look for the grey slender loris and other nocturnal animals by torchlight; sightings are never guaranteed.
newExperiences.where: Kandalama road, a few kilometres east of Dambulla
newExperiences.notes: Night-walk length from operator listings (1–1.5 h). Check whether night walks are run by NIFS staff or only by outside guides, and current hours.

newExperiences.name: Sri Maha Bodhi and the great stupas
newExperiences.shortDescription: See the sacred Bodhi tree and the white dome of Ruwanwelisaya at evening worship, among pilgrims dressed in white.
newExperiences.details: The Sri Maha Bodhi grew from a cutting of the tree under which the Buddha is believed to have attained enlightenment, brought here in the 3rd century BC. Nearby, Ruwanwelisaya rises about 100 m above a wall of carved elephants, and Thuparamaya is said to be the island's first stupa. Visit early or at evening worship; remove shoes and hats, and cover shoulders and knees.
newExperiences.season: Busiest on full-moon (poya) days, and at Vesak and Poson
newExperiences.notes: The living pilgrimage centre; distinct from the cycling card (ruins). Whether these sites are covered by the CCF ticket is unclear (Wikivoyage says the Bodhi tree and Ruwanwelisaya are free); the card avoids the point.

newExperiences.name: The sacred city by bicycle
newExperiences.shortDescription: Cycle the flat roads between Anuradhapura's ancient monasteries, from the Abhayagiri ruins to the vast brick stupa of Jetavanaramaya.
newExperiences.details: The ruins of the Abhayagiri and Jetavana monasteries spread over several kilometres north and east of the centre, linked by flat, shaded roads. A bicycle lets you stop at the Samadhi Buddha, the Kuttam Pokuna twin ponds, the moonstone at Mahasena's Palace and Jetavanaramaya. Bicycles can be hired in town; start early, as you walk barefoot at each site.
newExperiences.notes: Mirrors polonnaruwa-cycling. Owner: bicycles arranged or hired locally?

newExperiences.name: Mihintale
newExperiences.shortDescription: Climb the granite stairway to the hilltop where tradition says Buddhism came to Sri Lanka, with stupas and wide views over the plains.
newExperiences.details: A stairway of about 1,840 granite steps climbs to the hill where tradition says the monk Mahinda met King Devanampiya Tissa in the 3rd century BC. The way up passes the ruins of a monastery hospital and leads to stupas and the rock of Aradhana Gala. Go early or late in the day, and expect to remove shoes at the shrines. Most people take 2–3 hours.
newExperiences.where: Mihintale, about 12 km east of Anuradhapura (around 20–30 minutes by road)
newExperiences.season: Busiest at the Poson full moon, usually in June
newExperiences.notes: Step count 1,840 vs 1,850; fee about LKR 500–1,000 (not stated). Where shoes must be removed on the climb: confirm locally.

newExperiences.name: Aukana Buddha
newExperiences.shortDescription: See the 5th-century standing Buddha, nearly 12 m tall and carved from the living rock, facing the ancient Kala Wewa reservoir.
newExperiences.details: Carved from a granite rock face in about the 5th century, the standing Buddha at Aukana is nearly 12 m tall and still a place of worship, overlooking the Kala Wewa reservoir. A visit takes about half an hour; remove shoes and hat, and cover shoulders and knees. It is a detour of about an hour from Anuradhapura or Dambulla, often made on the drive between them.
newExperiences.where: Aukana, about an hour by road south of Anuradhapura, near Kala Wewa
newExperiences.notes: Could sit under dambulla instead (similar distance). Height 11.36–11.84 m across sources. Temple charges a small fee (not stated).

newExperiences.name: Wilpattu National Park safari
newExperiences.shortDescription: A half- or full-day jeep safari in Sri Lanka's largest national park, around forest lakes, looking for leopards, sloth bears and elephants.
newExperiences.details: Wilpattu's dry-zone forest is dotted with villus, shallow lakes that fill with rain, where leopards, sloth bears, elephants, deer and water birds come to drink. Drives on sandy tracks start from the main gate at Hunuwilagama; a half day covers the nearer lakes, a full day goes deeper. It is quieter than Yala, but sightings are never guaranteed, and heavy rain can flood the tracks and close the park.
newExperiences.where: Hunuwilagama gate, roughly 40–50 km west of Anuradhapura (about 1–1.5 hours by road)
newExperiences.season: Usually best about February to October; heaviest rain about October to January
newExperiences.notes: Candidate recommendation: Wilpattu as an excursion from Anuradhapura, not its own page. srilanka.travel's season line reads 'February and October' (probably 'February to October'). Road time is an estimate (official 30 km is straight-line to the park). 2025: 164,925 visitors (76,389 foreign). Closed 28 Nov–3 Dec 2025 (Ditwah); tourists stranded by floods near Eluwankulama 19 Oct 2025; drought in Aug 2026 with unrepaired eastern tanks.

existingExperiences.reason: The current text calls the city '11th-century' next to the Gal Vihara carvings, which are 12th-century; the city was the capital from 1070 for about two and a half centuries. Category 'history' is right.

newExperiences.name: Ancient city and Gal Vihara
newExperiences.shortDescription: Explore the medieval royal city: the palace walls, the circular Vatadage in the Quadrangle and the Buddha figures carved from one granite face.
newExperiences.details: Polonnaruwa was the royal capital from 1070 for about two and a half centuries. The ruins run several kilometres north from the museum, where tickets are sold: the royal palace, the Quadrangle with its Vatadage and Hatadage, Rankoth Vehera, Lankatilaka and the four Buddha images of Gal Vihara. A full morning covers the main groups; start early, before the heat.
newExperiences.notes: Overlaps with polonnaruwa-cycling; included so travellers who won't cycle can still select the main sight (as Sigiriya has its main sight as a card). Drop if you prefer one card.

newExperiences.name: Medirigiriya Vatadage
newExperiences.shortDescription: A quiet 7th-century circular relic house on a low rock, ringed by three circles of slender stone pillars, north of Polonnaruwa.
newExperiences.details: Built in about the 7th century, the vatadage at Medirigiriya stands on a low rock reached by a short flight of steps, with three rings of slender octagonal pillars around a small stupa and Buddha images. It is among the best-preserved buildings of its kind and usually has few visitors. Allow about half an hour on site; the rock gets very hot at midday.
newExperiences.where: Medirigiriya, about 35 km north of Polonnaruwa (around 45 minutes to an hour by road)
newExperiences.notes: Department of Archaeology site; no official page found. Distance 25–40 km across sources (34 km most specific). Low demand but a well-regarded hidden gem; keep or drop as you see fit.

newExperiences.name: Elephant safari: Minneriya or Kaudulla
newExperiences.shortDescription: An afternoon jeep safari from Polonnaruwa to see wild elephants on the reservoir grasslands of Minneriya or Kaudulla. Never guaranteed.
newExperiences.details: Minneriya's entrance is about 25–30 km west of Polonnaruwa, and Kaudulla lies to its north; the same herds use both, so drivers choose the park on the day. From about July to October elephants graze the drying reservoir beds, usually peaking around August and September. Many visitors see the ruins in the morning and take a safari of about 3 hours in the afternoon.
newExperiences.where: Minneriya or Kaudulla National Park, about 30–60 minutes by road from Polonnaruwa
newExperiences.season: Best about July–October; usually peaks around August–September
newExperiences.notes: OPTIONAL duplicate of sigiriya-elephant-safari for travellers based in Polonnaruwa or Giritale. The experience guide links to the Sigiriya id only.

candidates.recommendation: Better as an excursion/experience under Anuradhapura (proposed: anuradhapura-wilpattu-safari). A destination page only if the business later sells lodge stays or a western route (airport–Kalpitiya–Wilpattu–Anuradhapura).
candidates.summary: Sri Lanka's largest national park (about 1,317 km²), dry-zone forest dotted with villus (rain-filled natural lakes), known for leopards, sloth bears and elephants. No town: visitors come on half- or full-day jeep safaris from Anuradhapura or stay in lodges near the gates. 2025: 164,925 visitors, 76,389 foreign — about the same as Minneriya, far below Yala and Udawalawe. Quieter than Yala. Floods closed parts of the park in October–December 2025; drought stressed it in August 2026.
attractions: Leopards, sloth bears, elephants, water buffalo, mugger crocodiles
Hunuwilagama main gate (Anuradhapura side) and Eluwankulama gate (Puttalam/Kalpitiya side)
candidates.routes: Hunuwilagama gate roughly 40–50 km by road from Anuradhapura, about 1–1.5 h (estimate; official 30 km is straight-line). About 180 km from Colombo, roughly 4–5 h from the airport. Eluwankulama gate about 75–80 km from Kalpitiya (1.5–2 h, estimate). The coastal road through the park stays closed to public traffic (Supreme Court case ended May 2025).
candidates.season: Usually best about February to October; animals concentrate at the villus in the driest months (about May–September). Heavy north-east monsoon rain about October–January can flood tracks and close the park. Sightings never guaranteed.
ownerQuestions: Does Eranorris cover Wilpattu at all (jeep safaris arranged or booked locally; half or full day)?

candidates.recommendation: Its own destination page, medium priority. Too far for an excursion from any existing destination (about 4–5 h from Anuradhapura, 7–8 h from the airport); enough distinct sights for 2–3 nights; strong official promotion; rail and air access restored in 2026. Not high priority because foreign demand and room supply are still small.
candidates.summary: Cultural capital of the Tamil north: Hindu kovils (Nallur Kandaswamy and its 25-day festival, usually late July–September), the Portuguese/Dutch fort, the rebuilt public library, Keerimalai springs, Point Pedro, Casuarina Beach and ferry-reached islands (Nainativu, Delft). Jaffna Fort had 249,913 visitors in 2025 but only 14,532 foreign (Sigiriya: 582,687 foreign); Jaffna district has 757 registered rooms, and SLTDA calls the north a 'Northern Gap'.

candidates.routes: By road: Anuradhapura about 197 km (usually 4–5 h with a stop, estimate); Trincomalee about 230 km (4.5–5.5 h); Sigiriya about 254 km (5–6 h); airport about 360 km (7–8 h). Rail: Northern Line fully reopened 9 April 2026; from 10 July 2026 the Colombo–KKS intercity runs Friday–Monday only, the Night Mail and Yal Devi continue, with frequencies changed several times during 2026 (re-check). Flights: Chennai and Tiruchirappalli–Jaffna (IndiGo). KKS–Nagapattinam ferry seasonal (usually paused about November–February; November 2026 status unverified).
candidates.season: Dry zone; most rain about October–December (November usually wettest); drier January–September, hottest about April–August. Nallur festival usually late July–September, dates set by the temple.

candidates.recommendation: Its own destination page at low priority, or not needed for now. It does not work as an excursion (2.5–3 h each way from Anuradhapura or the airport, with early dolphin-boat departures). Build it only if the business wants kitesurfers or a western route via Wilpattu.
candidates.summary: A peninsula between the Puttalam lagoon and the sea: spinner-dolphin trips and sperm whales offshore (about November–April), the Bar Reef marine sanctuary, and Sri Lanka's main kitesurfing lagoon (main wind season about May–September). Niche demand: the Bar Reef sold tickets to 3,732 foreign visitors in 2025 (dolphin trips may not all be counted); SLTDA calls it 'a niche but growing market'.
attractions: Dolphin and whale watching (DWC 2012 sea-mammal regulations apply)
Kitesurfing on the Kalpitiya lagoon and at Kappalady
Mangroves, islands, salt pans of the Puttalam lagoon
Dutch fort (Navy-occupied, restricted) and Dutch church
candidates.routes: About 130–140 km from the airport (usually 2.5–3.5 h, estimate), 2.5–3 h from Negombo, about 120 km and 2.5–3 h from Anuradhapura; Wilpattu's Eluwankulama gate about 1.5–2 h.
candidates.season: Dolphins/whales about November–April; kite season about May–September/early October, with a lighter season about December–February; calmest sea about December–April.
